{"id": "6e4078a0-90d4-4b4f-829c-88cf4a0c4e37", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "tool_summary", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "tooluse_CB20c61VumFhg0mHUhVFaJ", "status": "success", "content": [{"text": "{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"Quotas for the bedrock-runtime endpoint\",\"context\":\"## Requesting a quota increase\\n\\nThe steps for requesting a quota increase for your account depend on the value in the **Adjustable** column in the quotas table in Amazon Bedrock service quotas.\\n\\n**Important:**\\n\\nBefore requesting a quota increase, verify that the model is not in a *Legacy* or *Deprecated* lifecycle status. Quota increases are not granted for models that are scheduled for retirement. Check the model's lifecycle status on the Model lifecycle page and consider migrating to the successor model instead.\\n\\n* If a quota is marked as **Yes**, you can adjust it by following the steps at Requesting a Quota Increase in the Service Quotas User Guide.\\n* For any model, you can request an increase for the following quotas together:\\n\\n + Cross-Region InvokeModel tokens per minute for `${model}`\\n + On-demand InvokeModel tokens per minute for `${model}`\\n + Cross-Model Max Tokens Per Day\\n\\n To request an increase for any combination of these quotas, request an increase for the **Cross-Region InvokeModel tokens per minute for `${model}`** quota by following the steps at Requesting a Quota Increase in the Service Quotas User Guide. After you do so, the support team will reach out and offer you the option of also increasing the other two quotas.\\n\\n **Note:**\\n\\n Due to overwhelming demand, priority will be given to customers who generate traffic that consumes their existing quota allocation. Specific models have non-adjustable fixed quotas. Availability varies by model and AWS Region. Check the model's detail page for Reserved Tier support and the Provisioned Throughput support table for availability. To access Reserved Tier, contact your AWS account team.\\n* Request for quota increase by contacting your account manager or AWS Support if your workload traffic exceeds your account quotas\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/troubleshooting-api-error-codes.html\"},{\"rank_order\":4,\"title\":\"bedrockruntime\",\"context\":\"## type ThrottlingException \\n\\n```\\ntype ThrottlingException struct {\\n RespMetadata protocol.ResponseMetadata `json:\\\"-\\\" xml:\\\"-\\\"`\\n\\n Message_ *string `locationName:\\\"message\\\" type:\\\"string\\\"`\\n // contains filtered or unexported fields\\n}\\n```\\n\\nYour request was throttled because of service-wide limitations. Resubmit\\nyour request later or in a different region. You can also purchase Provisioned\\nThroughput (<https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prov-throughput.html>)\\nto increase the rate or number of tokens you can process\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdk-for-go/api/service/bedrockruntime/index.html\"},{\"rank_order\":5,\"title\":\"Quotas for the bedrock-mantle endpoint\",\"context\":\"## How requests are evaluated against quotas\\n\\nWhen you submit an inference request to the `bedrock-mantle` endpoint, AWS evaluates it against your quotas in the following order:\\n\\n1. **Input tokens per minute** \u2013 The number of input tokens in the request, plus the value of `max_tokens` (or the model-specific maximum if `max_tokens` is not set), is checked against the input-tokens-per-minute quota for the requested model. If admitting the request would exceed the quota, the request is throttled with an HTTP 429 response.\\n2. **Output tokens per minute** \u2013 As the model streams or generates output, output tokens are counted against the output-tokens-per-minute quota for that model. If the quota is reached during generation, generation stops and the response is returned with a finish reason indicating the cutoff.\\n\\nAfter the response completes, any unused portion of the initial input-token reservation (the difference between `max_tokens` and the actual output) is replenished to your quota.\\n\\nThe endpoint may apply additional internal rate limiting that is not exposed in Service Quotas. Use retry logic with exponential backoff to handle transient throttling.\\n\\nThe `bedrock-runtime` endpoint's TPM quotas count input and output tokens together against a single per-model quota, while the `bedrock-mantle` endpoint applies separate input-tokens-per-minute and output-tokens-per-minute quotas. If you run workloads on both endpoints, plan capacity for each endpoint independently. For details on the runtime endpoint's quotas, see Quotas for the bedrock-runtime endpoint\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas-mantle.html\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Look up Bedrock quota increase documentation"}

{"id": "97190b46-a3ed-491a-a122-f15a629dd511", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Here's how to raise the quota, based on the current Bedrock documentation.

## Steps

1. **Find the throttled quota.** Open the Service Quotas console for Amazon Bedrock in the Region where you see the errors. Look for the per-model quotas:
   - On-demand InvokeModel tokens per minute for your model
   - On-demand InvokeModel requests per minute for your model
   - If you use a cross-Region inference profile, the cross-Region InvokeModel quota for that model
2. **Check the Adjustable column.**
   - **Yes:** request the increase directly in Service Quotas, using Request increase at account level.
   - **No:** the quota is fixed for that model. Open an AWS Support case or contact your account manager.
3. **Request the cross-Region quota to raise the related quotas together.** You can ask for any combination of these in one request:
   - Cross-Region InvokeModel tokens per minute
   - On-demand InvokeModel tokens per minute
   - Cross-Model Max Tokens Per Day

   File the request against **Cross-Region InvokeModel tokens per minute for your model**. AWS Support will then offer to increase the other two as well.
4. **Include these details in the request:**
   - Model ID and Region
   - Current quota value and the value you need
   - Your use case
   - Projected steady and peak requests and tokens per minute
   - Average input and output tokens per request

## Things that affect approval
- **Legacy or deprecated models:** increases aren't granted for models scheduled for retirement. Consider moving to the successor model.
- **Usage history:** AWS gives priority to customers whose traffic already consumes their existing quota. A request can be denied if you aren't using what you have.
- **New accounts:** these often start with lower quotas than the defaults.

## While you wait
- Add retries with exponential backoff and jitter. Throttling often comes from bursts.
- Lower `max_tokens` where you can. For `bedrock-runtime`, the request's token reservation counts against your tokens-per-minute quota.
- For steady, predictable load, consider Provisioned Throughput, or Reserved Tier if your model supports it. Reserved Tier is arranged through your account team.
- Use a cross-Region inference profile to spread load, if it fits your data residency requirements.

I can also check which quota you're hitting. For that I'd need your Region and model ID. With those I can compare your current quota values against actual usage in CloudWatch, which makes the request stronger. If you want, I can also submit the quota increase request for you, and it will need your approval before it runs.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
